summary: Platform tarball ships WebRTC remote-execution agent binary
details: sextant-cli-linux-arm64 is a platform-specific artifact package with no lifecycle scripts, no main, and no bin entry — it exists only to be resolved as an optional dependency of the parent sextant-cli package, which then invokes the shipped binary. The tarball contains a single 12MB Linux/arm64 Go ELF at bin/sxt. Strings in the binary show it statically links pion/webrtc, pion/dtls, pion/sctp, pion/turn, pion/stun, coder/websocket, and go-qrcode, and contains an internal executor symbol with transport.Direct and executor.nc references — the composition of a WebRTC data-channel remote-execution agent (peer-to-peer signaling, NAT traversal via STUN/TURN, QR-code pairing, arbitrary command executor), not the positioning/measurement tool the package name suggests. The package.json license field points at https://github.com/ddos798/claude_control, whose repository name and account handle directly reference remote-control / DDoS tooling and are inconsistent with a legitimate CLI utility. When the parent CLI invokes bin/sxt on the operator's host, the binary opens a WebRTC channel through which a remote peer can execute commands on that host.

cwes.description: The product contains code that appears to be malicious in nature.
cwes.name: Embedded Malicious Code
